Indicator_Name: Multi-taxa terrestrial and freshwater species abundance indicator (753 species)
Units_Measure: Index (1970=100); geometric mean across 753 species; % change since baseline
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 pp.12–13; Figure 1; Key Findings – Change in species' abundance
Data_Source: BTO Breeding Bird Survey; UKBMS; Wetland Bird Survey; National Bat Monitoring Programme; Rothamsted Insect Survey; bespoke species surveys
Climate_Rationale: Composite of schemes including weather-sensitive taxa (butterflies, bats, birds); inter-annual climate variability propagates into the headline figure
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Broader than JNCC C5/C6/C8 — explicitly combines birds, mammals, butterflies, moths, wetland birds across 753 species; SoN uses same underlying data but constructs a distinct composite indicator for reporting

Indicator_Name: Moth abundance index (broader countryside moths)
Units_Measure: Index (1970=100); % change; based on light trap counts
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 p.13; Figure 2A – Moth abundance
Data_Source: Rothamsted Insect Survey (RIS) light trap network; Butterfly Conservation Garden Moth Scheme
Climate_Rationale: Light trap catches are strongly influenced by temperature and moonlight; moth flight activity is directly temperature-dependent; counts vary substantially with night-time weather conditions
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not in existing sheets — moths are not covered by JNCC UKBI, EIF or Biodiversity Indicators sheets as a distinct abundance index

Indicator_Name: Rare and colonising bird species abundance index
Units_Measure: Index; % change since baseline; ~species with <1,000 UK breeding pairs
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 p.13; Figure 2D – Rare/colonising breeding birds
Data_Source: BTO Breeding Bird Survey; JNCC single-species surveys and SCARABBS
Climate_Rationale: As for other BBS-derived indices — weather affects counts but is not explicitly corrected for in this sub-indicator
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Distinct from common bird indices in other sheets — captures recovery of rare/colonising species separately from common bird abundance trends

Indicator_Name: Terrestrial mammal abundance index (15 species)
Units_Measure: Index; % change since 1998 baseline; 15 species
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 p.13; Terrestrial mammals section
Data_Source: Mammal Society / PTES National Mammal Atlas; BTO Breeding Bird Survey mammal records; camera trap surveys
Climate_Rationale: Weather is a background driver of mammal population dynamics; not directly used in index calculation
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Broader multi-species mammal indicator; JNCC C8 covers bats only — this covers 15 terrestrial mammal species including dormice, hedgehog, water vole

Indicator_Name: Amphibian and reptile distribution index
Units_Measure: Index of change in proportion of occupied 1-km squares; % change since baseline
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings; Appendices – Amphibians and reptiles
Data_Source: Amphibian and Reptile Conservation (ARC); National Amphibian and Reptile Recording Scheme (NARRS); NBN Atlas records
Climate_Rationale: Occupancy modelling of recording scheme data; climate affects distribution (amphibians sensitive to rainfall and temperature) but is not a direct model input
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not in existing sheets — SoN 2023 reports 31% of amphibian and reptile species at extinction risk; no dedicated A&R distribution index in JNCC UKBI or other sheets

Indicator_Name: Demersal fish abundance index (North Sea, 105 species)
Units_Measure: Index (1990s baseline); % change; mean abundance across 105 demersal fish species
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings – Marine section; pp.22–24
Data_Source: ICES North Sea International Bottom Trawl Survey (NS-IBTS); Celtic Sea IBTS surveys
Climate_Rationale: Sea surface temperature affects demersal fish distribution and catchability; embedded in survey catchability but not formally corrected for
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Distinct from EIF C7/C11 and JNCC B2 which focus on commercially exploited stocks — SoN uses a broader multi-species demersal community index including non-commercial species

Indicator_Name: Cetacean abundance index (whales and dolphins, 3 species)
Units_Measure: Index; % change since early 1990s; 3 cetacean species
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings – Marine section; p.24
Data_Source: ORCA / Joint Cetacean Protocol; SCANS surveys; Cetacean Research Programme
Climate_Rationale: Survey detections may be affected by sea state (weather) which limits visual observation; standard protocol corrects for effort but not weather conditions per se
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not in existing sheets — cetacean abundance as a distinct marine species group indicator is new to SoN and not covered in JNCC UKBI, EIF or other sheets

Indicator_Name: Grey Seal population abundance
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Marine & Fisheries | Governance, Society & Data
Units_Measure: Number of individuals; population growth rate (%/year)
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings – Marine; p.24
Data_Source: SMRU (Sea Mammal Research Unit) national seal surveys; statutory monitoring programme
Climate_Rationale: Population monitoring via aerial surveys; weather affects survey feasibility but SMRU applies effort correction; not formally weather-adjusted
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not separately tracked as an indicator in existing sheets — only seabird abundance is in the JNCC/EIF sheets; seal population is a distinct marine mammal indicator

Indicator_Name: Harbour Seal population abundance
Units_Measure: Number of individuals; % change by region
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings – Marine; p.24
Data_Source: SMRU national harbour seal surveys; aerial haul-out counts
Climate_Rationale: As for Grey Seal — survey effort correction applied but indicator is not weather-adjusted
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not in existing sheets — complementary to Grey Seal but showing contrasting regional trends; important indicator of marine mammal conservation status

Indicator_Name: Invertebrate distribution index (4,979 species)
Units_Measure: Index of change in proportion of occupied sites; average % change since 1970; covers insects, spiders, millipedes etc.
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings; pp.14–17
Data_Source: Biological recording schemes collated via NBN Atlas; UKCEH annual occupancy estimates (Outhwaite et al. 2019); Bayesian occupancy models
Climate_Rationale: Occupancy modelling uses UKCEH Bayesian methods on NBN Atlas recording data; climate is embedded in species' distribution dynamics and may appear in detection probability models
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Covers 4,979 invertebrate species far exceeding JNCC's butterfly/pollinator sub-sets; particularly highlights functional groups (pollinators −18%, pest controllers −34%, freshwater nutrient cyclers +64%)

Indicator_Name: Pollinator distribution index (bees, hoverflies, moths)
Units_Measure: Index of % change in occupied sites; average −18% since 1970 across pollinator species
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings; pp.14–15 – Pollination functional group
Data_Source: Bees/Hoverflies: UKCEH Bayesian occupancy models on NBN Atlas records; Moths: Rothamsted Insect Survey + Garden Moth Scheme
Climate_Rationale: Occupancy models on biological recording data; climate affects pollinator range and phenology; may be captured in species-level distribution models used in the occupancy framework
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Distinct from PoMS pollinator abundance indicator (UKBI D1c) — this is a distribution/occupancy metric covering far more species; not covered in existing sheets as a dedicated distribution indicator

Indicator_Name: Predatory insect distribution index (pest control functional group)
Units_Measure: Index of % change in occupied sites; average −34% since 1970 for pest-control insects (e.g., ladybirds, ground beetles)
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings; p.15 – Pest control functional group
Data_Source: UKCEH Bayesian occupancy models on NBN Atlas biological recording data
Climate_Rationale: As for invertebrate distribution index — climate is embedded in occupancy modelling framework
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — New functional group metric not covered in any existing sheet — specifically tracks ecosystem-function-relevant invertebrate groups

Indicator_Name: Freshwater invertebrate distribution index (nutrient cycling functional group)
Units_Measure: Index of % change in occupied sites; average +64% since 1970 (initial decline then recovery) — mayflies, dragonflies, stoneflies
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings; p.15 – Freshwater nutrient cycling group
Data_Source: UKCEH occupancy models; British Dragonfly Society; Riverfly Partnership survey data; NBN Atlas
Climate_Rationale: Freshwater invertebrates are sensitive to temperature and flow (climate-driven); occupancy models embed these effects indirectly
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Distinct freshwater invertebrate metric not in existing sheets — EIF B7 covers fish, not invertebrates specifically

Indicator_Name: Vascular plant (flowering plant) distribution index
Units_Measure: % of species showing decline in occupied sites; 54% of ~1,500 flowering plant species declined since 1970
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings; pp.18–19
Data_Source: Botanical Society of Britain and Ireland (BSBI) Plant Atlas 2020 and earlier atlas data; NBN Atlas
Climate_Rationale: BSBI atlas data from tetrad/10-km square recording over decades; climate drives plant range changes but mapping data are not weather-adjusted
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — JNCC Plants indicator (new 2025) covers 4 NPMS habitat types but is not yet assessed; SoN uses BSBI atlas data for a far larger species set; distinct from JNCC plant indicator

Indicator_Name: Bryophyte (mosses and liverworts) distribution index
Units_Measure: % of species declining in occupied sites; 59% of bryophyte species declined since 1970 (GB)
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings; p.19
Data_Source: British Bryological Society (BBS) recording data; NBN Atlas; UKCEH occupancy models
Climate_Rationale: Distribution data from recording schemes; climate affects bryophyte moisture requirements and range but not a direct model input
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not covered in any existing sheet — no dedicated bryophyte indicator in JNCC UKBI, EIF or Biodiversity Indicators sheets

Indicator_Name: Lichen and fungi distribution index
Units_Measure: % of species declining in occupied sites; 28% of fungi/lichen species at extinction risk
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings; p.19 and Red List section
Data_Source: British Lichen Society; British Mycological Society; NBN Atlas recording data
Climate_Rationale: Recording scheme data; fungi and lichen distributions affected by air quality and climate but not weather-adjusted in occupancy models
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not covered in any existing sheet — no dedicated lichen or fungi indicator in JNCC UKBI, EIF or Biodiversity Indicators sheets

Indicator_Name: UK species extinction risk assessment — GB Red List (10,008 species assessed)
Units_Measure: % threatened with extinction from GB; 16% threatened, 2% (151 spp) already extinct in GB since 1500
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings – Extinction risk; pp.20–21
Data_Source: JNCC and country nature conservation body Red List assessments; IUCN criteria applied at GB scale across 10,008 species
Climate_Rationale: GB Red List assessments. Aggregates IUCN Red List category changes. Climate change is a recognised threat driver, but assessments are expert status classifications: no climate data enter the calculation and weather does not move the annual value (Legend 1, rule B).
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Distinct from IUCN global Red List Index in existing sheets — this is a GB-scale Red List assessment across a much wider species set (10,008 species) than the IUCN global RLI; coverage of fungi, lichens, invertebrates exceeds existing sheets

Indicator_Name: UK Overseas Territories species extinction risk (6,557 species assessed)
Units_Measure: % of UKOT species threatened with global extinction; 11% of 6,557 species assessed threatened
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – UK Overseas Territories and Crown Dependencies section; pp.166–180
Data_Source: IUCN Red List global assessments for UKOT-endemic and resident species; BirdLife International; JNCC UKOT programme
Climate_Rationale: UKOT Red List assessments. Aggregates IUCN Red List category changes. Climate change is a recognised threat driver, but assessments are expert status classifications: no climate data enter the calculation and weather does not move the annual value (Legend 1, rule B).
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Partially covered by JNCC K3 indicator (Red List Index for UKOTs) but SoN provides a broader absolute count across 6,557 species; distinct metric

Indicator_Name: Northern Ireland species extinction risk (2,508 species assessed)
Units_Measure: % threatened with extinction from island of Ireland; 12% (281 species) at risk
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 Key Findings – Northern Ireland extinction risk; p.20
Data_Source: Northern Ireland Environment Agency (NIEA); CEDaR; IUCN criteria applied at island-of-Ireland scale
Climate_Rationale: NI Red List assessments. Aggregates IUCN Red List category changes. Climate change is a recognised threat driver, but assessments are expert status classifications: no climate data enter the calculation and weather does not move the annual value (Legend 1, rule B).
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Distinct geographic subset not covered separately in existing sheets — JNCC indicators report UK-level; NI-specific risk assessment is additional detail

Indicator_Name: State of Nature Watchlist Indicator (155 priority species)
Units_Measure: Index of average abundance change for 155 high-priority conservation species; % change since baseline
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – new 2023 indicator; Conservation Response section
Data_Source: Multi-scheme data (BTO BBS, UKBMS, NBMP, Rothamsted, single-species surveys) for 155 species on UK Red/Amber lists or Biodiversity Action Plan lists
Climate_Rationale: Composite of monitoring schemes including weather-sensitive taxa; climate variability propagates into the index as for other multi-taxa composites
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — New indicator introduced in SoN 2023 — not covered in existing sheets; distinct from JNCC priority species abundance (C4a) which uses a different species selection methodology

Indicator_Name: UK priority habitat condition assessment — all priority habitats
Units_Measure: % of assessed priority habitat area in good condition; 14% (1 in 7) in good condition
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – Conservation Response section; pp.36–107 habitat assessments
Data_Source: Natural England; NatureScot; NRW; NIEA; SSSI / NNR condition monitoring; Phase 2 habitat surveys
Climate_Rationale: Field-survey-based condition assessment; weather at survey time is background influence not formally used
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Broader than JNCC SSSI condition (A3c) — this covers all priority habitats assessed against good condition criteria, not just designated sites

Indicator_Name: Woodland habitat condition (% in good condition)
Units_Measure: % of woodland assessed as in good ecological condition; 7% of woodland in good condition
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – Conservation Response; woodland habitat section
Data_Source: Forestry Commission; Natural England woodland condition assessments; National Forest Inventory condition data
Climate_Rationale: Condition assessment from field surveys; weather is background influence not formally used
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — More specific than JNCC B1b (certification) — SoN reports ecological condition, not just sustainability certification; a distinct metric

Indicator_Name: Peatland habitat condition (% in good condition)
Units_Measure: % of peatland area in good condition; 25% of peatlands in good condition; ~75% damaged or degraded
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – Conservation Response; peatland section
Data_Source: Natural England; NatureScot; NRW; NIEA; condition monitoring programmes; JNCC peatland surveys
Climate_Rationale: Peatland condition surveys; hydrological condition is rainfall-dependent but survey methodology is not weather-adjusted
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — More specific condition metric than existing sheets — JNCC EIF E7 (healthy soils) is broader; SoN reports specifically on peatland ecological condition as a headline metric

Indicator_Name: Seafloor Good Environmental Status (Marine Strategy Framework Directive)
Units_Measure: % of assessed seafloor meeting Good Environmental Status; 0% meeting GES due to bottom-trawling disturbance
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – Conservation Response; marine section; p.96
Data_Source: JNCC; Marine Management Organisation; ICES seabed mapping; bottom-trawling pressure data (VMS vessel monitoring)
Climate_Rationale: Based on VMS trawl pressure mapping and habitat condition surveys; weather affects trawling effort marginally but not the condition assessment methodology
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — More specific than EIF C9/C2 — SoN explicitly reports the shocking headline that 0% of UK seafloor meets GES due to fishing disturbance; not in existing sheets as a distinct indicator

Indicator_Name: Peatland restoration rate (ha restored per year)
Units_Measure: >5,000 ha of degraded peatland restored per year (UK); comparison to target
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – Conservation Response; peatland restoration section
Data_Source: Natural England; NatureScot; NRW; NIEA; National Lottery Heritage Fund peatland programmes
Climate_Rationale: Administrative reporting of restoration area from scheme records; no climate data used in calculation
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not in existing sheets — while JNCC tree planting and agri-environment scheme area are covered, peatland restoration area per year as a standalone metric is not included in any existing sheet

Indicator_Name: Seagrass bed extent and restoration area
Units_Measure: Hectares of seagrass present; ha restored per year; decline in distribution since historical baseline
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – Conservation Response; seagrass section
Data_Source: Natural England; NRW; Ocean Conservation Trust; Project Seagrass mapping surveys
Climate_Rationale: Seagrass extent from survey/remote sensing; sea temperature affects seagrass growth (climate influence) but is not formally used in extent mapping
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not in existing sheets — seagrass is not covered in any existing sheet as a distinct habitat metric; a notable gap given SoN highlights it as a key blue carbon restoration habitat

Indicator_Name: Biodiversity Intactness Index (BII) — UK
Units_Measure: % of original natural biodiversity remaining; UK BII ~50%; indicating >50% of original biodiversity lost due to human activity
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – Summary and introductory section; pp.8–9
Data_Source: Natural History Museum PREDICTS database; land-use and human pressure data; modelled using PREDICTS framework across plants, fungi, invertebrates and vertebrates
Climate_Rationale: PREDICTS-based BII is modelled from land-use intensity; climate is at most a secondary covariate and not an input to the published index (Legend 1, rules B and G; aligned with [BIP-052], [IPBES-N-037], [GBF-047]).
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not directly in existing sheets — the IPBES/CBD ecosystem integrity index is related but BII is a distinct modelled indicator based on the NHM PREDICTS database; SoN 2023 uses it as a headline contextual figure

Indicator_Name: Proportion of large fish in commercial landings (fish stock health proxy)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Marine & Fisheries | Trade & Industry
Units_Measure: % of large (older) fish in total landings; increasing trend since 2002 cited in SoN 2023
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – Conservation Response; sustainable fisheries section; p.54
Data_Source: ICES stock assessment data; UK fishing vessel catch returns (MMO); length-frequency data from port sampling
Climate_Rationale: Fish growth rates are temperature-dependent; sea temperature affects the age/size structure of fish populations; embedded in population dynamics rather than directly input to the landing-size calculation
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not in existing sheets — SoN uses this as a novel indicator of fishing sustainability beyond the standard MSY metrics in EIF C10 and JNCC B2; proportion of large/old fish in landings reflects ecosystem-level recovery

Indicator_Name: Proportion of farmland in agri-environment schemes (of any type)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Governance, Society & Data
Units_Measure: % of UK farmland in agri-environment schemes; ~20% (one-fifth); improving trend over 20 years
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – Conservation Response; nature-friendly farming section; p.45
Data_Source: Defra; Welsh Government; Scottish Government; DAERA agri-environment scheme statistics
Climate_Rationale: Administrative scheme registration data; no climate data
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — JNCC B1a covers higher-level/targeted agri-environment schemes specifically; SoN reports all agri-environment scheme participation (including entry-level/basic tier); a wider metric

Indicator_Name: Species trend comparison: protected vs unprotected areas
Units_Measure: Relative index showing species trends inside vs outside protected areas; some evidence of more positive trends inside PAs
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – Conservation Response; protected areas section; pp.72–85
Data_Source: BTO BBS; UKBMS; NBN Atlas occupancy models stratified by protected area status
Climate_Rationale: Trend data from monitoring schemes; weather affects counts similarly inside and outside PAs; climate is a background influence not formally corrected for
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not in existing sheets — this is a novel conservation effectiveness metric comparing trends inside and outside PAs; distinct from JNCC protected area extent or condition metrics

Indicator_Name: Agricultural intensification pressure index
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Biosecurity
Units_Measure: Composite index of agricultural intensification (fertiliser use, pesticide use, tillage, drainage) as a driver of biodiversity change
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – Historical Change section; pp.30–35; driver analysis
Data_Source: Defra BSFP; EUROSTAT agri-environment statistics; Countryside Survey land-cover data
Climate_Rationale: Composite of activity data; no climate data directly used in pressure index calculation
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not in existing sheets as a composite — individual components (pesticide use, nitrogen) are in Biodiversity Indicators sheet from JNCC/Defra sources, but SoN constructs a composite agricultural pressure index

Indicator_Name: Inequality in access to nature (socio-economic gradient)
Units_Measure: Measure of difference in proximity to and use of nature-rich spaces between socio-economic groups; people in deprived areas have less access
Policy_Goal: State of Nature Partnership; UK Biodiversity Indicators; GBF
Source_Reference: SoN 2023 – Conservation Response; co-ordinating our response section; p.107
Data_Source: Natural England Monitor of Engagement with Natural Environment (MENE); Index of Multiple Deprivation; GIS spatial analysis of greenspace access
Climate_Rationale: Survey and spatial analysis data; no climate data
Framework_Classification: No – NEW — Not in existing sheets — a socio-ecological equity metric unique to SoN among the sources covered; EIF G4 covers overall engagement but not the inequality dimension
